description:
Configure two independent Docker Compose projects to communicate via external networks. 

Scenario: You have a 'shared-infra' project (PostgreSQL + Redis) and a 'flask-api' project. Currently, they cannot talk to each other because they are on isolated default networks.

Your task:
1. Create two external Docker networks named 'infra-db-net' and 'infra-cache-net'.
2. Modify '/home/ga/Documents/docker-projects/shared-infra/docker-compose.yml' to attach Postgres to 'infra-db-net' and Redis to 'infra-cache-net'.
3. Modify '/home/ga/Documents/docker-projects/flask-api/docker-compose.yml' to attach the API service to BOTH networks.
4. Ensure all networks are declared as 'external: true' in the compose files.
5. Start all services using Docker Compose.
6. Verify connectivity by running the Flask app's health checks (http://localhost:5050/health/db and /health/redis).
7. Save a brief report to '/home/ga/Documents/docker-projects/connectivity-report.txt' confirming the networks created and the status of the connections.
